examples.problem_statement: In a class, the ratio of female to male students is 6:27. Reduce the ratio to its simplest form

solution.description: The problem states the ratio of female to male students is 6:27

solution.operation: Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 6 and 27
solution.description: The largest number that divides both 6 and 27 is 3

solution.operation: Divide both terms by the GCD
solution.description: Dividing both terms by their GCD simplifies the ratio to its lowest terms
Check the result: 2 and 9 share no common factor greater than 1, so 2:9 cannot be reduced any further and is the simplest form.

examples.problem_statement: A gear wheel having 128 teeth is in mesh with a 48-tooth gear. What is the gear ratio?

solution.description: Write the gear ratio straight from the tooth counts given in the problem: 128 teeth on the first wheel compared with 48 teeth on the second.

solution.operation: 128 and 48 can both be divided by 2, i.e. 128:48 is the same as 64:24
solution.description: Both numbers are even, so divide each term by 2; the ratio 128:48 describes the same comparison as 64:24.

solution.operation: 64 and 24 can both be divided by 8, i.e. 64:24 is the same as 8:3
solution.description: 64 and 24 share the larger common factor 8, so divide both terms by 8 and the ratio becomes 8:3.

solution.operation: There is no number that divides completely into both 8 and 3 so 8:3 is the simplest ratio
solution.description: Check for any remaining common factor: nothing divides into both 8 and 3, so 8:3 is the simplest form of the gear ratio.

examples.problem_statement: A wooden pole is 2.08 m long. Divide it in the ratio of 7 to 19

solution.operation: Since the ratio is 7:19, the total number of parts is 7 + 19 = 26 parts.
solution.description: Add the two ratio terms to see how many equal parts the pole is being divided into: 7 + 19 gives 26 parts.

solution.operation: 26 parts corresponds to 2.08 m = 208 cm, hence, 1 part corresponds to $\frac{208}{26} = 8$.
solution.description: Work in centimetres so the division stays in whole numbers: 2.08 m is 208 cm, and dividing 208 by 26 shows that one part is 8 cm.

solution.operation: Thus, 7 parts corresponds to $7 \times 8 = 56$ cm and 19 parts corresponds to $19 \times 8 = 152$ cm.
solution.description: Scale one part up to each of the two pieces: 7 parts is 7 times 8, or 56 cm, and 19 parts is 19 times 8, or 152 cm.

examples.problem_statement: In a competition, prize money of £828 is to be shared among the first three in the ratio 5:3:1

solution.operation: Since the ratio is 5:3:1 the total number of parts is 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 parts.
solution.description: Add the three ratio terms to find how many equal shares the prize money is split into: 5 + 3 + 1 gives 9 parts.
Those 9 equal parts together make up the whole prize fund of 828 pounds.

solution.operation: 1 part corresponds to $\frac{828}{9} = £92$, 3 parts corresponds to $3 \times £92 = £276$ and 5 parts corresponds to $5 \times £92 = £460$.
solution.description: Divide 828 by 9 to value one part at 92 pounds, then multiply up: 3 parts is 276 pounds and 5 parts is 460 pounds.

examples.answer: Hence, £828 divides in the ratio of 5:3:1 as £460 to £276 to £92.

examples.problem_statement: A map scale is 1:30000. On the map the distance between two schools is 6 cm. Determine the actual distance between the schools, giving the answer in kilometres

solution.operation: Actual distance between schools = $6 \times 30000$ cm = 180000 cm
solution.description: A scale of 1:30000 means every centimetre on the map stands for 30000 cm on the ground, so multiply the 6 cm map distance by 30000 to get 180000 cm.
Convert that actual distance from centimetres to metres by dividing by 100, which gives 1800 m.
Convert metres to kilometres by dividing by 1000, so the two schools are 1.80 km apart.

examples.answer: (1 mile ≈ 1.6 km, hence the schools are just over 1 mile apart.)

examples.problem_statement: Express 45 p as a ratio of £7.65 in its simplest form

solution.operation: Changing both quantities to the same units, i.e. to pence, gives a ratio of 45:765
solution.description: Put both amounts into the same unit before comparing them: 7.65 pounds is 765 pence, so the comparison becomes 45:765.
Both terms are divisible by 5, so divide each by 5 and the ratio 45:765 reduces to 9:153.
9 and 153 share the factor 3, so divide both terms by 3 to get 3:51.

solution.operation: Dividing both quantities by 3 again gives 3:51 ≡ 1:17
solution.description: Divide both terms by 3 once more to reach 1:17, which has no common factor left and is the simplest form.

examples.problem_statement: 20 tonnes of a mixture of sand and gravel is 30% sand. How many tonnes of sand must be added to produce a mixture which is 40% gravel?

solution.operation: Amount of sand in 20 tonnes = 30% of 20 t = $\frac{30}{100} \times 20 = 6$ t.
solution.description: Find how much of the 20 tonne mixture is sand: 30 percent of 20 t is 30 over 100 times 20, which is 6 t.

solution.operation: If the mixture has 6 t of sand then amount of gravel = 20 - 6 = 14 t.
solution.description: Everything that is not sand is gravel, so subtract the sand from the total: 20 minus 6 leaves 14 t of gravel.

solution.operation: We want this 14 t of gravel to be 40% of the new mixture. 1% would be $\frac{14}{40}$ t and 100% of the mixture would be $\frac{14}{40} \times 100$ t = 35 t.
solution.description: Adding sand does not change the amount of gravel, so treat that 14 t as 40 percent of the new mixture: 1 percent is 14 over 40 tonnes, and the whole mixture is 14 over 40 times 100, or 35 t.

solution.operation: If there is 14 t of gravel then amount of sand = 35 - 14 = 21 t.
solution.description: Split the new 35 t mixture into its two parts: taking away the 14 t of gravel leaves 21 t of sand in the finished mixture.

solution.operation: We already have 6 t of sand, so amount of sand to be added to produce a mixture with 40% gravel = 21 - 6 = 15 t.
solution.description: Compare that requirement with the 6 t of sand already present, so the sand that must be added is 21 minus 6, which is 15 t.

examples.problem_statement: Hooke’s law states that stress, σ, is directly proportional to strain, ε, within the elastic limit of a material. When, for mild steel, the stress is 63 MPa, the strain is 0.0003. Determine (a) the value of strain when the stress is 42 MPa, (b) the value of stress when the strain is 0.00072

solution.operation: (a) Stress is directly proportional to strain. (i) When the stress is 63 MPa, the strain is 0.0003
solution.description: Part (a) begins from the measured pair for mild steel: a stress of 63 MPa goes with a strain of 0.0003, and the two quantities are in direct proportion.

solution.operation: (ii) Hence, a stress of 1 MPa corresponds to a strain of \frac{0.0003}{63}
solution.description: Scale that pair down to one unit of stress, so a stress of 1 MPa corresponds to a strain of 0.0003 divided by 63.

solution.operation: (iii) Thus, the value of strain when the stress is 42 MPa = \frac{0.0003}{63} × 42 = 0.0002
solution.description: Scale the unit strain back up to the stress asked for by multiplying by 42 MPa, which gives a strain of 0.0002.

solution.operation: (b) Strain is proportional to stress. (i) When the strain is 0.0003, the stress is 63 MPa.
solution.description: Part (b) reverses the roles of the two quantities, reading the same measured pair as a strain of 0.0003 going with a stress of 63 MPa.

solution.operation: (ii) Hence, a strain of 0.0001 corresponds to \frac{63}{3} MPa.
solution.description: Work with a convenient small strain: 0.0001 is one third of 0.0003, so it corresponds to one third of 63 MPa.

solution.operation: (iii) Thus, the value of stress when the strain is 0.00072 = \frac{63}{3} × 7.2 = 151.2 MPa.
solution.description: The strain asked for, 0.00072, is 7.2 times 0.0001, so multiply that stress by 7.2 to get 151.2 MPa.

examples.problem_statement: Charles’s law states that for a given mass of gas at constant pressure, the volume is directly proportional to its thermodynamic temperature. A gas occupies a volume of 2.4 litres at 600 K. Determine (a) the temperature when the volume is 3.2 litres, (b) the volume at 540 K

solution.operation: (a) Volume is directly proportional to temperature. (i) When the volume is 2.4 litres, the temperature is 600 K.
solution.description: Part (a) begins from the measured pair for the gas: a volume of 2.4 litres goes with a temperature of 600 K, and volume is directly proportional to temperature.

solution.operation: (ii) Hence, a volume of 1 litre corresponds to a temperature of \frac{600}{2.4} K.
solution.description: Scale that pair down to one litre, so a volume of 1 litre corresponds to a temperature of 600 divided by 2.4 kelvin.

solution.operation: (iii) Thus, the temperature when the volume is 3.2 litres = \frac{600}{2.4} × 3.2 = 800 K.
solution.description: Multiply that per-litre temperature by the 3.2 litres asked for, giving a temperature of 800 K.

solution.operation: (b) Temperature is proportional to volume. (i) When the temperature is 600 K, the volume is 2.4 litres.
solution.description: Part (b) reverses the roles, reading the same measured pair as a temperature of 600 K going with a volume of 2.4 litres.

solution.operation: (ii) Hence, a temperature of 1 K corresponds to a volume of \frac{2.4}{600} litres.
solution.description: Scale down to one kelvin, so a temperature of 1 K corresponds to a volume of 2.4 divided by 600 litres.

solution.operation: (iii) Thus, the volume at a temperature of 540 K = \frac{2.4}{600} × 540 = 2.16 litres.
solution.description: Multiply that per-kelvin volume by the 540 K asked for, giving a volume of 2.16 litres.

examples.problem_statement: Change the following to index form: (a) 32 (b) 625

solution.operation: To express 32 in its lowest factors, 32 is initially divided by the lowest prime number, i.e. 2.
solution.description: To write 32 in index form, break it into prime factors, starting with the smallest prime that divides it, which is 2.
32 divided by 2 is 16, so 32 can be written as 2 times 16.

solution.operation: 16 is also divisible by 2, i.e. $16 = 2 \times 8$. Thus, $32 = 2 \times 2 \times 8$.
solution.description: 16 is even as well, so 16 is 2 times 8, and therefore 32 is 2 times 2 times 8.

solution.operation: 8 is also divisible by 2, i.e. $8 = 2 \times 4$. Thus, $32 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 4$.
solution.description: Split the 8 in the same way, since 8 is 2 times 4, giving 32 as 2 times 2 times 2 times 4.

solution.operation: 4 is also divisible by 2, i.e. $4 = 2 \times 2$. Thus, $32 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$.
solution.description: One more split finishes the factorisation, since 4 is 2 times 2, leaving 32 as five factors of 2.
Count those five equal factors and write them as a single power, so 32 in index form is 2 to the power 5.

solution.operation: 625 is not divisible by the lowest prime number, i.e. 2. The next prime number is 3 and 625 is not divisible by 3 either. The next prime number is 5.
solution.description: Now start again with 625, testing the primes in order: it is not divisible by 2, nor by 3, so move on to the next prime, 5.
625 divided by 5 is 125, so 625 can be written as 5 times 125.

solution.operation: 125 is also divisible by 5, i.e. $125 = 5 \times 25$. Thus, $625 = 5 \times 5 \times 25$.
solution.description: 125 is divisible by 5 too, giving 125 as 5 times 25, so 625 is 5 times 5 times 25.

solution.operation: 25 is also divisible by 5, i.e. $25 = 5 \times 5$. Thus, $625 = 5 \times 5 \times 5 \times 5$.
solution.description: 25 splits into 5 times 5, which leaves 625 written entirely as four factors of 5.
Count those four equal factors and write them as a single power, so 625 in index form is 5 to the power 4.
